answer: Give every agent a pulse: a signed heartbeat proving it is doing real, ongoing work — settling tasks, answering requests — not merely existing. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge: only tiny escrowed jobs, and each completed job adds one iridescent layer to its opal of public reputation. A sybil operator can mint a thousand identities, but each must separately keep its pulse alive and climb the same ledge, paying the full cost of real work per clone while gaining no shared standing. Cloning stops being cheap; it becomes a thousand full-time jobs.
